findings.summary: The one behaviour the M0.7 acceptance criterion names explicitly -- the base-ref resolution 'step that FAILS rather than defaulting to a range that examines nothing' -- has zero test of any kind. It is plain bash (a case statement plus two guard conditions), not GitHub Actions machinery, and the claim 'GitHub Actions cannot be executed locally, nothing asserts anything about ci.yml' is broader than the truth: this specific block can be extracted to a script and run under T0 with no socket, clock or object store, exactly the signal testing.md rule 1 names for logic in the wrong layer. I extracted lines 66-79 verbatim into a standalone script and exercised it in seconds against this tree: push with a real `before`, push with `before` = 40 zeros (branch creation), push with an orphaned SHA absent from a shallow/fetch-depth-0 checkout (force-push), schedule with no `before` at all, pull_request with a real base, and a synthetic single-commit (root) repo on schedule. All six matched the documented behaviour (fail closed on the force-push and root-commit cases, resolve HEAD~1 otherwise) -- so the logic itself is currently correct, but nothing in the tree constrains it going forward. A predicate this shape is idiomatic here already: buildSrc/src/test/java/binjava/ModuleGateTest.java stages a scratch git repo and drives a gate script through its production entry point for exactly this reason.
findings.failure_scenario: Any of three edits leaves the tree green forever, because nothing executes ci.yml and nothing executes an extracted equivalent: (a) change the final `|| { echo ...; exit 1; }` to `|| true`, negating the exact criterion this task exists to satisfy; (b) delete the `git cat-file -e "$base^{commit}"` existence check, so a force-push's orphaned SHA is accepted as-is and CHECK_RANGE points at a commit this checkout does not have, which downstream tools resolve however they resolve an unreachable ref rather than failing; (c) change `*) base=$(git rev-parse HEAD~1 ...)` to `*) base=HEAD`, so on the schedule trigger CHECK_RANGE becomes a self-diff (empty range) and every range-reading gate silently examines nothing and reports ok -- the precise failure mode this backlog task exists to prevent, now failing open instead of closed. None of the three trips a gate, a test, or a doc check; the only thing that would notice is a human reading the diff of a future PR.

findings.summary: Not part of the staged diff, so not blocking M0.7 on it, but directly relevant to why this gap wasn't surfaced by default routing: `code=$(printf '%s\n' $paths | grep -cE '\.(java|kt|kts|sh|py)$|\.pre-commit-config' ...)` does not match `.github/workflows/*.yml`, so this exact commit was routed to the 'documentation consistency -- No code changed. Do NOT review for code defects' lens only, and never to 'would this test fail if the code were wrong' or 'a gate that reports success while checking nothing' (line 32's case also does not match this path). ci.yml is executable shell wrapped in YAML and is itself an enforcement artifact (it decides which pre-commit hooks run in CI, with a SKIP list) -- the same class of file line 33's lens exists for. This is a two-file predicate (extend the regex to include `.github/workflows/.*\.ya?ml$`), so per non-negotiable 9 it belongs in the script, not in a reviewer's judgement each round.
findings.failure_scenario: A future edit to ci.yml's Gates step or its SKIP list is reviewed under the docs-only lens by default, which explicitly instructs the reviewer not to look for code defects -- the same routing gap that let an always-failing pre-commit --hook-stage commit-msg step ship in an earlier round of this exact task and required a reviewer to notice by running the command by hand rather than being prompted to.
